label: Fukuoka Airport
note: Land at nine, collect the car at ten. Kurokawa is only 1 h 45 m away direct, so the afternoon is yours.

label: Mameda-machi, Hita
note: A preserved Edo merchant street of white-walled townhouses. An hour is enough.

label: Nabegataki Falls
note: A wide, low curtain of water you walk behind. Ten minutes from the house.

label: Kurokawa · DeepSpot
note: Three bedrooms, private sauna, Aso panorama, 10 min drive from the village. €222 for four. Buy the tegata pass for the baths.
leg: 1 h 59 m from Fukuoka via Hita and the falls

label: Daikanbo
note: The northern rim of the caldera, looking down the whole crater floor. The Milk Road runs along the ridge from here.

label: Nakadake · Kusasenri
note: The live crater and the grass plain below it. November gate hours are 8:30–17:00.
status: Cancelled if gas is high — check at breakfast

label: Amano-Iwato
note: The cave the sun goddess hid in, plus the river cave at Amanoyasugawara filled with thousands of stacked stone cairns.

label: Takachiho · the gorge
note: Yokagura danced at Takachiho Shrine at 20:00, about an hour, every night. Dinner in town beforehand. The self-row boat to Manai Falls goes at opening the next morning.
when: 18 Nov · evening, and again at dawn

label: Aoshima
note: Rakuten STAY HOUSE x WILL STYLE, room 102: three bedrooms, kitchen, free parking, €174. The island shrine and the Devil's Washboard are a fifteen-minute walk from the door, not a drive.

label: Udo Jingu
note: A vermilion shrine built inside a sea cave in the cliff face. The most striking single thing on this coast.

label: Obi, Nichinan
note: An intact samurai castle town, the turning point of the coast day before you turn back north to Aoshima.

label: Kagoshima Airport
note: Car back at 13:00, flight at 17:00, then four nights in Osaka to the 24th. The four hours between have a free thermal footbath and a view of Sakurajima.
leg: 1 h 34 m from Aoshima direct, 1 h 58 m with the three stops

label: Dazaifu Tenmangu
note: A major shrine 30 min out of Fukuoka, and about thirty shops along its approach grilling umegae mochi to order — red bean inside, plum-blossom stamped on a hot iron plate.

label: Kurume
note: Where tonkotsu ramen was invented, at a stall called Nankin Senryo in 1937. The milky white broth came a decade later, by accident, when a cook at Sankyu left the pot on too long.

label: Kumamoto Castle
note: Reopened August 2026 after the earthquake, with new stone-wall damage and reconstruction running to 2052. Sakuranobaba Josaien at its foot is the easiest lunch of the day; Suizenji Jojuen garden is a short hop.

label: Kikuchi Gorge
note: Four kilometres of clear water and moss under broadleaf forest, and one of Kumamoto's best autumn walks. Closed after the quake, entry ban since lifted.
leg: 11 min of driving, an hour of walking

label: Gokase
note: An old house rented whole: three bedrooms, two toilets, kitchen, free parking. Check in around 17:00, then it is 16 minutes back into Takachiho for dinner and the kagura.

label: Sekinoo Falls
note: Potholes among the largest in the world, a National Natural Monument since 1928, plus suspension bridges over the gorge. Free entry and parking. 30 min for the falls, 50 with the potholes, 60 for the full loop.
leg: 4 min on top of the Kirishima detour

label: Kirishima Jingu
note: A shrine in deep cedar forest on the volcano's flank, twenty minutes from the airport.

label: Kareigawa Station
note: Opened 1903 and the oldest wooden station building in Kyushu, a National Registered Cultural Property since 2006. Original waiting room and ticket counter. Ten minutes from the airport, so it is the natural last stop.
leg: 4 min on top of the other two

label: Cape Toi
note: Wild horses grazing on an open headland at the southern end of the Nichinan coast.
when: 19 Nov · if you sleep at Nichinan
